nodes.label: Stratified Isolation Forest Analysis
nodes.rationale: The survey recommends stratifying anomaly detection by Base CBG and hospital class, with fallback strata for sparse groups.

nodes.label: Balanced Bagging XGBoost
nodes.rationale: Parallel XGBoost models should pair all positive examples with balanced negative subsamples while avoiding synthetic clinical records from SMOTE or ADASYN.

nodes.label: SHAP Auditor Reason Codes
nodes.rationale: TreeSHAP contributions must be translated into three readable reasons for each high-risk claim.

nodes.label: Stratified Isolation Forest
nodes.rationale: Grouping by Base CBG and hospital class prevents naturally expensive complex procedures from being mislabeled as anomalies.

nodes.label: Module Encapsulation Plan
nodes.rationale: Separating agents, core services, state, RAG, ML, and verification scripts is proposed to avoid spaghetti code and align module contracts.

nodes.label: Clinical Incoherence Indicators
nodes.rationale: Sepsis or shock claims paired with outpatient care or very short inpatient stays without ventilator or vasopressor support are treated as incoherent patterns.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Fallback Strategy
nodes.rationale: Sparse strata fall back from Base CBG plus Kelas RS to broader clinical and service-level groups, then global scoring.

nodes.label: Clinical Incoherence Features
nodes.rationale: Comorbidity and care-intensity inconsistencies, such as sepsis with no ICU stay and very short LOS, are intended fraud signals.

nodes.label: LangGraph Multi-Agent Orchestration
nodes.rationale: A Validator must assess ML and Qdrant evidence while an Executor produces a structured formal adjudication draft.

nodes.label: Qdrant Semantic RAG
nodes.rationale: Semantic search over INA-CBG and PNPK PDF rules is required to retrieve precise medical rules from narrative claims.
